clusters.text: Late night political drama as Peña is impeached and arrested Paraguay's President Santiago Peña has been impeached and placed under house arrest after a bank collapse triggered a crisis that left more than half of the country's population without access to their accounts. Peña was arrested on Friday minutes after lawmakers, including from his own party, unanimously voted to remove him from office following the collapse earlier this week of Ueno Bank, which has links to his private business interests. He had offered to step down on Thursday. Rather than accept his resignation, senators impeached Peña and charged him with misconduct, meaning he has been stripped of the immunity usually granted to ex-presidents. Peña, who until last year held shares in the company that owned the bank, has denied any wrongdoing. The impeachment charges that led to Peña's removal alleged he had conflicts of interest, manipulated regulatory oversight, diverted pension funds, and participated in an institutional cover-up involving the central bank. He is due to be questioned on Saturday over allegations of breach of trust, influence peddling, and misappropriation of funds, prosecutor Silvia Margarita Gonzalez Vester said. Peña's deputy, Pedro Alliana, has been sworn in as the new interim president and promised not to "abandon" the millions of people affected by the scandal. "Compatriots who are now going through a difficult time as a result of the financial collapse will be fully compensated," said Alliana, who will serve as president until 2028. The demise of the digital bank left more than half of Paraguay's population without access to their savings after it was seized by Paraguay's central bank. Long lines of people trying to withdraw money from Ueno branches snaked down the streets of the capital Asuncion on Tuesday and Wednesday. An estimated three million depositors remain unable to access their savings and pensions, prompting public outrage particularly in the capital, Asunción. Protests erupted across the country in response, with thousands taking to the streets on Thursday to demand their money. Earlier demonstrations featured clashes with the police, who used tear gas and water cannons on the crowd. Peña's impeachment passed with 44 out of 45 senators voting in favour of it. clusters.text: The Kristaps Porziņģis saga has followed the Golden State Warriors around since the very first day of training camp. And while it seems like it will stay in the news cycle for quite a while, on Friday it took another step towards resolution, with the one-time All-Star posting a statement on social media, which seemed to suggest that he is retiring. [Media: https://twitter.com/kporzee/status/2118813584784330754?a=9hOM4_a_iQis9uQx99s&s=20] The statement, which he signed and labeled “official statement,” reads in full as follows: > This season I was really looking forward to running it with this group, but as I ramped up, my body didn’t respond the way I anticipated. > I’m doing good, but I know what it takes, and I’m not where I want to be to perform at the level that I expect from myself. At this point, I’ve made the decision to prioritize my health and step away from the game I love. > In this situation, I want to show the utmost respect for the Golden State Warriors and work with them to find a solution that makes sense. > I’m thankful to my family and close ones for always being there. Much appreciation to all of you for the support. > Onwards and upwards. Porziņģis’ statement is in line with all the reporting in recent days. Earlier today, our Marc Delucchi wrote about the reports that Porziņģis had played his last game with the team, and all that was left was to handle a trade for a player who was unlikely to ever play again. That came after news earlier in the week that Golden State was withholding payments towards Porziņģis’ $20 million salary, and that neither Porziņģis nor the Players Association had plans to contest that. So now what? It appears that Porziņģis is set to retire, but first wants to help out the Warriors. By remaining an active player — even an unpaid one — Porziņģis retains his cap hold which can be used to facilitate a trade. The Warriors can now attempt to trade Porziņģis’ contract to a team in search of an expiring deal, and willing to offer a longer-term contract in exchange, such as the Milwaukee Bucks with Myles Turner, to name one of the many players the Dubs have been linked to. After Porziņģis’ contract is used to facilitate a trade — likely sooner rather than later — he can formally announce his retirement.

OpenAI plans to expand access to all Daybreak Red customers soon. clusters.text: People stopped for minor traffic violations will no longer be referred to US Immigration and Customs Enforcement. The mayor of Houston, the most populous city in the US state of Texas, has ordered the city’s police force to sharply limit its cooperation with the United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). John Whitmire’s executive order came on Friday, days after Democrats swept statewide offices in the traditionally Republican state. According to the order, Houston police will contact ICE only when a person is being arrested for a jailable offence, according to the Reuters news agency. Whitmire said he had consulted Texas’s newly elected governor, lieutenant governor and comptroller before acting, and that the move was meant to reduce fear and anxiety across the city. “Elections matter,” Whitmire told reporters. “I do this to begin a healing process,” he said, adding he hoped his executive order would become a model for other Texas cities. Joining Whitmire at the news conference, Houston Police ⁠Chief J Noe Diaz said he supported the change and that his department had already begun to implement the new policy. Under the new rules, people stopped for minor traffic violations will no longer be referred to ICE simply because they have an administrative immigration warrant. The decision reverses a policy Whitmire put in place in April under pressure from outgoing Republican Governor Greg Abbott. Abbott had threatened to withdraw about $110m in state public safety grants, arguing that a city council ordinance limiting police contact with ICE breached Senate Bill 4, a 2017 state law that bars local police from restricting cooperation with federal immigration authorities. Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton also sued the mayor, the city council and the police chief over the ordinance. “We’re taking an interpretation of the law today, working with the newly elected members of the state leadership, in implementing this policy,” Whitmire told reporters. “We don’t want people to worry about ⁠their workers, their family members, their students.” The issue has drawn intense scrutiny in Houston. The arrest Thursday night happened after secret service officers approached a man “acting suspicious” in a parked car, according to a Homeland Security statement. US officials said the suspect – Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos – went on to describe voices in his head that were telling him to come to the nation’s capital and kill the Republican president. Shortly after, officers discovered the suspect’s vehicle had been reported stolen and he had three firearms and dozens of rounds of ammunition. This is the latest in a series of arrests the secret service and other law enforcement agencies have made against individuals who have threatened Trump or his family members’ lives since he returned to office last year. Debris from Saturday’s attack damaged a residential building, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. “Explosions in the Kyiv suburbs. The attacks come as Zelenskyy said his government is seeking specific guarantees from Western allies on how post-war security support would function. Officials said the programme, covering 37 agricultural export clusters across Uttar Pradesh, will begin on November 23 and be conducted in three phases.The initiative aims to equip farmers with the skills and knowledge to export their produce directly, reducing dependence on intermediaries who often take a substantial share of the profits, said Dr Dinesh Chandra, assistant agriculture marketing officer, Prayagraj division.He said farmers from all export-oriented clusters were being trained in export procedures and documentation so they could independently access overseas markets.The first phase, scheduled from November 23 to 27, will be held at the National Institute of Agricultural Marketing (NIAM), Jaipur, where farmers will learn agricultural marketing processes. clusters.text: NEW DELHI: A Delhi consumer commission has ordered an airline to pay Rs 71,587 to a passenger who missed his Bengaluru-bound flight after allegedly being delayed by ground staff at the airport.The commission found that the airline had failed to substantiate its claim that the passenger reported late for check-in. It noted that the carrier had not produced supporting evidence, such as CCTV footage, to establish that he had arrived after the stipulated time.The New Delhi District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, headed by president Poonam Chaudhry and member Bariq Ahmad, directed the airline to refund Rs 11,587, which the passenger spent on booking another ticket on the same day. It also awarded him Rs 50,000 for mental agony, harassment and humiliation, and Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses.The dispute arose after the passenger booked a round-trip journey from Delhi to Bengaluru, with his onward flight scheduled for June 22, 2025, and his return journey on June 28. He told the commission that he had made the booking a month in advance as he needed to attend an urgent official meeting in Bengaluru.According to his complaint, he reached Delhi airport at around 5.45am, an hour before his scheduled departure at 6.45am. However, he alleged that airline staff took more than 45 minutes to process his check-in despite repeated requests for assistance.He further claimed that a ground staff member incorrectly informed him that the flight was full and asked him to approach the help desk for rescheduling. The process was further delayed when another staff member allegedly behaved rudely and directed him from one employee to another.By the time the matter was addressed, he had missed his flight. clusters.text: Ranchi Jamshedpur: Markets brimmed with cheer on Friday as residents stepped out in numbers to buy gold, silver, utensils, vehicles, earthen diyas and firecrackers on Dhanteras.High prices of gold failed to deter customers as jewellery stores in Ranchi and Jamshedpur witnessed a steady stream of customers since morning. In Ranchi, traders estimated sales of precious metals, electronics, real estate, utensils and festive items to the tune of Rs 700 crore. In Jamshedpur, the figure breached Rs 500 crore-mark.“Ranchi’s Dhanteras business was over Rs 700 crore and festive sales across the state are expected to touch around Rs 2,300 crore,” Tulsi Patel, president of Federation of Jharkhand Chamber of Commerce and Industries (FJCCI), said.In Ranchi, 24-carat gold was priced at Rs 1,42,040 per 10 grams while 22-carat gold stood at Rs 1,30,203. The rate for 20-carat gold was Rs 1,18,367 and 18-carat gold was Rs 1,06,530 per 10 grams. Silver (999 purity) was priced at Rs 1,83,860 per kg. Despite the high rates, jewellery stores witnessed heavy footfall throughout the day.“Gold and silver sales crossed Rs 150 crore. Customers purchasing gold and silver coins also turned up in large numbers throughout the day,” Jitendra Verma, president of Ranchi Sona Chandi Vyavsayi Samiti said.Over 600 cars were sold citywide on Friday. “We wanted to buy something auspicious without stretching our budget.
